I started about a year ago and my garden went to hell in a handbasket pretty quickly. Here are a few things I learned:

- Use good soil even if that means you need to purchase a truck of organic compost. Tilled up clay just doesn't cut it.

- I thought I needed a tiller, I didn't. I needed good soil. 4 smaller raised beds with premium organic soil are all I am planting this year.

- figure out your watering situation. Rain barrels, hoses, working faucets, etc. It is all great until you hit July 8th and get a 15 day dry spell.

- plant less and care more. I thought that if I had a greater number of seedlings, that the quantity would make up for any mistakes or lack of proper weeding. This was incorrect. I had a lot of seedlings that failed to thrive and mostly died.

- weed

- you are looking for 'thriving' plants. If you are not seeing lots of growth, you are having an issue.

- orange oil can be a natural pesticide. If I had any plants worth protecting, that would have been something I would have tries.

- you will mess up. That is part of the experience, don't beat yourself up.

- don't be in a hurry to get things in on the frost date. Yeah, you want to get things in, but if it is still a muddy mess, the slugs will eat all of your vines and pumpkins.

- Seeds are actually super cheap Jan to March because you can get year old seeds from the 2019 season. My local place has a fire sale in March to make room for the new inventory.
